title: OpenAI Responses behavioral mapping: stream ordering, tool-call fidelity, and schema-drift mitigation
creator: Asha Rao
description:
Background: As we onboard more user traffic that expects OpenAI Responses compatibility, we continue to see behavioral mismatches in three areas: (1) streaming event ordering and partial-event boundaries, (2) function/tool-calling envelopes (start/args/end semantics and nested tool-call cycles), and (3) structured output schema drift (missing/renamed fields and partial JSON chunks). These mismatches cause customer-facing regressions (failed tool invocations, truncated JSON outputs, or non-deterministic ordering) when routing requests to Redwood-hosted variants or when using the compatibility translation layer.

Goal: Define, implement, and canary a translation shim that maps OpenAI Responses streaming events to Redwood's internal streaming model with deterministic ordering, canonical tool-call envelopes, and best-effort structured output repair. The shim must be togglable per-customer and have observability and fallbacks to avoid increasing error surface area.

Scope: Implementation targets the hosted API translation path and the Dedicated gateway for a first pass. Private/VPC will be covered by configuration only (no code changes) in this ticket. Non-goals: full ONNX-level kernel changes, deep tokenization normalization for non-UTF8 content (follow-up ticket).

Acceptance criteria:
- Translation shim available behind a runtime feature flag and configurable per-route.
- Passes parity harness: 100 curated end-to-end tests (stream chunks, function calls, nested tool cycles, and structured JSON outputs) with >=95% behavioral parity vs. reference OpenAI Responses behavior.
- CPU and tail-latency overhead under canary: median extra latency <= 12ms, P99 <= 120ms due to buffering.
- Metrics emitted: event_reorder_count, partial_json_repair_count, toolcall_mismatch_count, shim_buffering_time_ms; all instrumented in Console dashboards.
- Graceful fallback: on unrecoverable mismatch, shim returns a standardized error event that maps to Redwood error codes and increments a tracing span/trace with original payload.

High-level approach:
1) Canonical event model: define a small canonical vocabulary for chunk events (e.g., CHUNK_TEXT, CHUNK_JSON_PART, TOOL_CALL_START, TOOL_CALL_ARG, TOOL_CALL_END, TOOL_RESULT_PART, TOOL_RESULT_END, STREAM_END). Each incoming OpenAI event is mapped to one of these with a sequence-id assigned.
2) Ordering & sequencing: the shim assigns monotonic sequence IDs and emits events to the runtime in-order. For out-of-order arrival from upstream, buffer up to 500ms or 8 chunks (configurable) then emit with a reproducible gap indicator.
3) Tool-call envelope reconciliation: synthesize missing TOOL_CALL_END when we detect a following non-tool event or a nesting mismatch, preserving the original argument blob for debugging. If nested tool calls are observed where target runtime does not support nesting, flatten by queuing subcalls and annotate the top-level toolcall with "flattened_nested_calls" metadata.
4) Structured output repair: run lightweight json-schema validation against route-configured schemas. For partial JSON streams, accumulate until parseable or until a max buffer size (64KB). When minor schema drift detected (renamed keys, missing optional fields), apply best-effort transforms using a configurable mapping table. Emit audit events with transform_reason.
5) Observability and tracing: attach original event IDs to traces, surface repair diffs in Console, and add a Kibana/LogQL index for raw vs. translated events.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Buffering to enforce ordering improves parity but increases tail latency. The 500ms/8-chunk buffer is a pragmatic compromise; we'll tune in canary.
- Best-effort schema repair can mask customer bugs. We will introduce an opt-in "repair" mode per-customer; default is "detect-only" that surfaces issues to Console.
- Flattening nested tool calls loses original call interleaving; we only do this when target runtime lacks nesting and flag it in traces.

Test plan:
- Expand the existing responses compatibility harness (ENG-50321) with 100 new scenarios focusing on edge streaming and nested toolcalls. Test cases include: mid-chunk JSON boundary splits, early end events, duplicate TOOL_CALL_START, missing TOOL_CALL_END, tool call that returns streaming chunks, and tool result that contains multi-part JSON.
- Unit tests for canonicalizer and repair logic.
- Integration tests using a small dedicated cluster to measure latency overhead.
- Chaos test: drop random stream events upstream and verify shim emits consistent error event and recovery path.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0: deploy shim as disabled behind feature flag in runtime-1.20 in staging.
- Phase 1: internal canary (10% of internal traffic) for 48 hours; instrument metrics and logs.
- Phase 2: customer canary (5% of eligible customer traffic) for 1 week with "detect-only" repair mode.
- Phase 3: enable opt-in repair mode for select customers; monitor for 2 weeks.
- Phase 4: GA toggle to default to "detect-only" and provide migration guides for customers.

Monitoring & SLOs:
- Alert if event_reorder_count increases by >10x baseline or if shim_buffering_time_ms P99 > 250ms.
- Dashboard: per-route counts of repaired outputs and repair-failure rates, per-customer rollback link.

Docs & artifacts:
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/COMPAT/Responses+Event+Canonicalization (draft)
- PR template and initial implementation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7943
- Parity test suite repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compat-harness/tree/eng-261422
- Design notes and trade-off matrix: Google Drive doc https://drive.google.com/open?id=1Xq-example

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Q1: Default behavior for repair mode (detect-only vs auto-repair) for high-volume customers. Proposal: detect-only default, sales/SRE can opt-in customers to repair.
- Q2: Maximum buffering threshold per-customer: allow per-tenant override? Proposed: yes, but with tenant-pinned latency guardrails.
- Q3: Do we unify sequence IDs with existing runtime sequence field or use shim-local sequence? Proposal: unify where possible, but shim will present both shim_seq and runtime_seq during canary.

- ENG-50321 (responses-translation-heuristics-and-runtime-mismatch-playbook) - test harness and prior heuristics
- ENG-75210 (observability-instrumentation-streaming-events) - dashboards and metrics
- ENG-21456 (compat-shim-risk-register-openai-responses-parity) - risk list

notes: This ticket intentionally keeps repair mode opt-in to reduce customer impact. If canary metrics are within bounds, follow-up ticket will expand repair heuristics and schema mapping authoring UI.
